title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 8-K, second-quarter 2026 financial results (Item 2.02, Exhibit 99)
date_evidence: Date of Report (Date of earliest event reported) July 22, 2026 ... On July 22, 2026, GE Vernova Inc. (the "Company") released its second-quarter 2026 financial results on its investor relations website
key_claim: GE Vernova filed this Form 8-K on 22 July 2026. In Q2 2026 GE Vernova signed 20 GW of new gas equipment contracts, of which 18 GW were slot reservation agreements and 2 GW were orders; it converted 10 GW of existing slot reservation agreements to orders and shipped 3 GW, taking firm backlog from 44 to 53 GW and slot reservation agreements from 56 to 63 GW. Combined gas equipment backlog and slot reservation agreements grew from 100 to 116 GW, with at least 125 GW anticipated by year-end 2026, against annual gas turbine output of 20 GW rising to 24 GW in 2028 and 30 GW in 2030.
frame_summary: GE Vernova presents the combined backlog and slot reservation figure as evidence of durable demand and a raised guidance story, reporting the reservation and firm-order components separately in the segment detail rather than in the headline.
verbatim_quote: Signed 20 gigawatts (GW) of new gas equipment contracts, including 18 GW of slot reservation agreements and 2 GW of orders.

title: Earnings Release Q3 FY 2026: Siemens Energy accelerates profitable growth
key_claim: Siemens Energy reported record Q3 FY2026 orders of 17.9 billion euros and an order backlog of 162 billion euros, and attributed the increase in free cash flow before tax to 2,319 million euros partly to customer advance payments associated with the strong order intake.
frame_summary: Siemens Energy frames the quarter as evidence that capacity expansion and disciplined pricing are converting record demand into profit and cash, treating customer advance payments as a favourable working-capital effect rather than as a claim on future factory output.
verbatim_quote: Free cash flow pre tax increased to €2,319m (Q3 FY 2025: €419m). The sharp increase resulted largely from the improvement in cash-effective profit and was further supported by customer advance payments associated with the strong order intake.
verbatim_list: Orders reached another record level of €17.9bn.
Book-to-bill ratio (ratio of orders to revenue) was 1.57, while order backlog increased to €162bn at quarter-end.

title: The Queue Before the Queue: GEV's Backlog Extends to 2031
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-08-04T16:54:47+00:00 ... byBrynna Foley, Enverus Intelligence(R) Research August 4, 2026
key_claim: New combined-cycle gas turbine costs have risen more than 2x since 2020 with equipment lead times a key driver; in ERCOT a highly efficient CCGT requires a PPA of roughly $70/MWh to achieve bankable returns while the same asset in PJM requires a capacity price upwards of $400/MW-day; operational gas assets continue to transact at approximately half of replacement cost, so acquiring existing generation remains more attractive than building.
frame_summary: Enverus argues that the turbine queue has repriced the build-versus-buy decision, making acquisition of existing gas plants the rational route to near-term load growth exposure rather than new construction.
verbatim_quote: Operational assets continue to transact at approximately half of replacement costs. With new CCGT economics strained by supply chain constraints and rising prices, purchasing existing generation remains the more attractive path for companies seeking exposure to near-term load growth.
verbatim_list: New CCGT costs have risen more than 2x since 2020, with equipment lead times a key driver of that inflation.
GEV’s gas turbine backlog climbed to 116 GW in Q2, up from 100 GW in the prior quarter.

title: Procuring and Scaling Grid Flexibility
date_evidence: Report August 31, 2026 # Procuring and Scaling Grid Flexibility
key_claim: RMI and the Global Energy Alliance set out procurement guidance for grid flexibility and for making battery energy storage investable, on the argument that reliability needs can be translated into procurable services and met by resources other than new thermal plant.
frame_summary: RMI argues that reliability under load growth is a procurement-design problem rather than an equipment-supply problem, and that flexibility services and battery storage can meet system needs without waiting on new thermal capacity.
verbatim_quote: Battery energy storage systems, in particular, can support resource adequacy, system balancing, and system stability across multiple timescales.

title: Ansaldo Returns to U.S. Gas Turbine Market as Equipment Crunch Widens Supplier Field
key_claim: Across their July and August 2026 disclosures, four gas turbine manufacturers reported at least 157.6 GW in firm orders or contract backlog worldwide, rising to about 246.6 GW once GE Vernova's and Siemens Energy's slot reservation agreements are included. GE Vernova's 116 GW comprises 53 GW firm backlog and 63 GW under slot reservation agreements; Siemens Energy reported 69 GW firm and 26 GW reserved. Scott Strazik said the company's secured supply chain capacity was funded by customer down payments; Christian Bruch cited strict project selectivity; Hiroshi Nishio said Mitsubishi is being selective in the projects it contracts. Ansaldo Energia re-entered the US market with eight AE64.3A turbines, about 624 MW, for a Pacifico Energy data centre project in Texas.
frame_summary: POWER argues that a widening equipment crunch is drawing new suppliers into the US gas turbine market while the incumbents expand output, and it compiles the manufacturers' disclosures to show how much of the reported pipeline is reserved rather than ordered.

verbatim_list: GE Vernova reported 116 GW of gas turbine capacity under contract, up from a combined 100 GW three months earlier, including 53 GW in firm backlog and 63 GW under slot reservation agreements.
At quarter-end, Siemens Energy separately reported

we’ve now reached our 20 GW annualized run rate and are on track for 24 GW in 2028, we now see further opportunity to serve this growing demand with 30 GW of annual output in 2030 in a capital-efficient manner, utilizing lean and incremental machinery in our existing factory footprint and have already secured significant supply chain capacity, all funded by customer down payments
In the large-frame gas turbine market on which we focus, particularly among our core U.S. utility customers, we are being selective in the projects we contract.
And at the same time, we prioritize value over volume, maintaining strict project selectivity and pricing discipline.

The Italian manufacturer will supply California-based energy infrastructure developer Pacifico Energy with eight AE64.3A gas turbines and associated generators for a Texas power project supporting major data center infrastructure.

Increasing annual mid-sized turbine capacity from about 50 units in fiscal 2025 to about 100 in fiscal 2028, and large-turbine capacity from roughly 35 units in fiscal 2026 to more than 50 in fiscal 2028.
Targeting at least 30% higher GTCC shipments by fiscal 2028 and evaluating a subsequent increase of 50% or more.
GE Vernova noted an aeroderivative could be commissioned in about six months, while a heavy-duty turbine might require another 18 months of site work after shipment.
